Name: PackRat
Author: moomeowmeme
Description:
[size=6][b]PackRat[/b][/size]
[i]Know what you have, keep it tidy, and let the farm run itself.[/i]

PackRat is for players with forty chests and no idea which one has the Blueberry Wine. Press [b]P[/b] for a menu that shows everything you own, everywhere on your farm, and everything you don't have yet. It adds two self-stacking freezers, a Strongbox that locks, grabbers that do your harvesting and collecting overnight, a Machine Loader that fills a whole shed of machines in one click, a Storm Totem, and a recipe for the Auto-Petter. You can also put a short label on any chest.

[line]

[size=5][b]New in 1.1[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Machine Loader:[/b] say which machine each item goes in (or a whole group at once: All fruit, All mushrooms...), then fill every empty machine in the building at once. It can keep them filled too: whenever the grabber empties them, and whenever you close a chest there.[/*]
[*][b]Field Grabber:[/b] picks a whole quarter of the farm every night: crops, fruit trees, forage (your pigs' truffles too), honey, mushrooms and tapper goods. While you're placing one, the quarter it covers lights up.[/*]
[*][b]Storm Totem:[/b] a thunderstorm tomorrow, with far more lightning than usual. Lightning rods love it.[/*]
[*][b]Auto-Petter:[/b] now craftable.[/*]
[*][b]Move in:[/b] one button in the No Stars freezer moves a whole group of food in from your backpack.[/*]
[*][b]Strongbox:[/b] opens whenever the key is in your backpack; you don't need it in your hand.[/*]
[*][b]PackRat menu:[/b] items show the star of the best quality you have, and a new Grabbers tab shows where every grabber is and where one is missing.[/*]
[*][b]Settings:[/b] change any key, drag PackRat's buttons wherever you like, and turn on vegetarian mode.[/*]
[*]The Crop Grabber is retired. Yours turn into Field Grabbers (outdoors) or Greenhouse Grabbers (indoors) by themselves, contents and all.[/*]
[/list]
[line]

[size=5][b]The PackRat menu[/b][/size]
Press [b]P[/b], or click the PackRat button (a little packrat peeking out of a chest) on your backpack page or in any open chest.

[list]
[*][b]Everything in one place:[/b] every chest, freezer, fridge, mini-fridge, dresser, grabber, Auto-Grabber, Junimo chest, hopper and shipping bin, plus your backpack, what you're wearing, and the bait and tackle on your rods. Items you've donated to the museum or given to Community Center bundles count too.[/*]
[*][b]Every flavor on its own line:[/b] Blueberry Wine and Starfruit Wine are counted separately. So are each Jelly, Pickles, Juice, Dried Fruit, Dried Mushrooms, Honey, Roe, Aged Roe and Smoked Fish.[/*]
[*][b]Quality at a glance:[/b] each item shows the star of the best quality you have, and hovering it shows how many you have at normal, silver, gold and iridium quality.[/*]
[*][b]Where it is:[/b] the same hover lists which chests hold it, biggest first, using your chest labels.[/*]
[*][b]Find it:[/b] click an item to pin it, then click a chest row. A "Here!" marker bobs over that chest so you can walk straight to it.[/*]
[*][b]What you're missing:[/b] every item you don't have yet shows too, faded, including every possible flavor the game can make.[/*]
[*][b]Tabs and search:[/b] Crops & Forage, Artisan Goods (grouped into Wine, Jelly, Pickles and so on), Animal Products, Fish, Cooking, Minerals & Artifacts, Resources and Everything Else.[/*]
[*][b]Filters:[/b] show everything, only what you have, or only what you're missing; count only items of silver quality or better, gold or better, or iridium; count only one place, such as the Shed or the Cellar; only one kind of storage, such as your freezers or dressers; or only one type of item, such as vegetables, fruit, artifacts, geodes or wine. Sort by name, count or sale price.[/*]
[*][b]Grabbers tab:[/b] the last tab shows where every grabber is: the farm quarter by quarter, and each shed, barn, cellar or greenhouse with machines or crops. It warns you about a quarter or building without one, a grabber that's full, or two doubled up, and clicking a grabber puts a marker over it.[/*]
[*][b]Totals:[/b] how many kinds of item you have out of everything there is, how many items you're storing, in how many containers, and what it's all worth.[/*]
[/list]
It's built only from the game's own menu pieces (boxes, title scroll, inventory slots, tooltips, quality stars and sounds), so it looks like it shipped with the game.

[line]

[size=5][b]Storage[/b][/size]

[b]Bulk Freezers[/b]
Two freezers that each hold 70 slots, as much as a Big Chest, and count as a fridge, so you can cook with what's inside. They keep themselves tidy: matching stacks merge the moment something goes in.
[list]
[*][b]Bulk Freezer (Keep Stars)[/b] (cream): merges stacks and leaves quality alone. Gold Potatoes stack with gold Potatoes and normal with normal.[/*]
[*][b]Bulk Freezer (No Stars)[/b] (icy blue): first drops everything to normal quality, so all your Potatoes end up in one stack of 300 instead of four stacks by quality. Its [b]Move in[/b] button moves a whole group of food (vegetables, fruit, mushrooms, fish, eggs and milk, artisan goods you can eat...) in from your backpack at once.[/*]
[/list][color=#cc6600][b]The No Stars downgrade is permanent.[/b] Gold and iridium items lose their stars and their extra value. Keep your best items in the Keep Stars freezer or somewhere else.[/color]

[b]Strongbox[/b] (iron, with a brass padlock)
A locked box with [b]three pages of 70 slots: 210 in all[/b], three times a Big Chest. It only opens while the [b]Strongbox Key is in your backpack[/b]. The first time you try to open a Strongbox, you'll find a key taped to the lid, and that one key opens every Strongbox you own. Lose it, and Clint will make you a new one for 2,500g. It's in his shop whenever the key isn't in your backpack, so a key left in a chest, or locked inside a Strongbox, counts as lost.

[b]Chest labels[/b]
Give any chest a label of up to 3 characters, shown on a small parchment tag on its front. Point at a chest and press [b]L[/b], or open it and click the label button beside the chest menu. Leave the box blank to remove a label.

[line]

[size=5][b]Harvesting and machines[/b][/size]

[b]Field Grabber[/b] (brown, outdoors only)
The farm is split into four quarters at its middle (it works on any outdoor map, split the same way). Every night, a Field Grabber picks every ready crop and fruit tree in [b]its quarter[/b], picks up the forage lying there (truffles from your pigs too), and collects from its bee houses, mushroom logs and tappers (those as soon as they finish, day or night). Every other machine (kegs, jars, oil makers, worm bins, lightning rods...) is left for an [b]Artisan Grabber[/b]. Everything goes inside it (70 slots). While you're placing one, its quarter lights up green and a tag names it ("North-east quarter"); once it's down, a message confirms which quarter it covers, warns you if that quarter already has one, and names any quarters that still have none.

[b]Greenhouse Grabber[/b] (green, indoors only)
The same harvest for the [b]whole building[/b] it's standing in: every crop and every fruit tree. Put one in your greenhouse and never walk the rows again.

[b]Artisan Grabber[/b] (wine red)
It collects the finished goods from [b]every machine in the building[/b] it's standing in, overnight and through the day as each one finishes (it checks every 10 minutes): kegs, preserves jars, casks, dehydrators, cheese presses, looms, crystalariums, worm bins and the rest. Machines that restart on their own when emptied, such as crystalariums and bee houses, start their next batch just as if you'd collected by hand. Casks are collected once they reach iridium quality. Outdoors, it covers the whole outdoor area it's in, so one Artisan Grabber on the farm empties every outdoor keg, jar and oil maker there.

How the grabbers pick:
[list]
[*]Quality and yield follow the same rules as picking by hand: fertilizer and farming level count, one item per plant gets the quality roll and any extras are normal quality, and deluxe fertilizer still guarantees silver. Fruit tree quality comes from the tree's age.[/*]
[*]Sunflowers drop their seeds, wheat sometimes gives hay, and fiber sometimes gives mixed seeds, just like picking by hand.[/*]
[*]You get the same farming experience as picking by hand (in co-op, it goes to whoever placed the grabber, or to the host if they're offline).[/*]
[*]Forage follows the hand-picking rules too: your foraging level sets the quality (always iridium with Botanist), Gatherer can double it, and you get the foraging experience.[/*]
[*]Regrowing crops (blueberries, hops, coffee and so on) are left on the plant to regrow. Wild forage crops such as spring onions are left for you.[/*]
[*]A full grabber stops collecting, and the rest waits safely on the plant or in the machine.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Machine Loader[/b]
Walk into a shed full of machines and fill them all at once. Press [b]K[/b], or click the Load button (with a keg on it) in an Artisan Grabber.
[list]
[*]One row for each item in the chests here that a machine here will actually load, with how many you have. You can set an item before you have enough for a batch: with 3 coffee beans, set them to Keg now, and the row says a Keg needs 5. They go in as soon as there are 5 (with Keep machines filled, by themselves).[/*]
[*]Beside each item, a dropdown of [b]only the machines here that accept it[/b]: Blueberries offer Keg, Preserves Jar and Dehydrator; Hops offer only Keg; Milk offers only Cheese Press.[/*]
[*][b]Whole groups at once:[/b] rows at the top such as [b]All vegetables[/b], [b]All fruit[/b], [b]All mushrooms[/b], All fish, All eggs and All milk send every item of that kind to one machine, so you don't have to set each one. An item set to its own machine goes there instead (all fruit to kegs, but Ancient Fruit to jars), and an item set to Nothing is left out of its group. The Prismatic Shard and legendary fish are never part of a group, so they only go in a machine if you set them yourself.[/*]
[*]Rows fill from the top, so order is priority: use a row's little arrows to move Blueberries above Hops, and the kegs take blueberries first.[/*]
[*][b]Fill[/b] loads every empty machine the way you would by hand (a furnace takes its coal from the same chest as the ore; professions apply), lowest quality first so your best stays for selling. A line at the bottom says what went in and what ran out.[/*]
[*]It takes from chests only, [b]never your backpack[/b], so nothing you're carrying goes into a machine by surprise. To load something you're carrying, drop it into a chest there first: the Artisan Grabber is handy, since its Load button is right there. Indoors, it takes from every chest in the building, freezers and grabbers included (not Strongboxes or mini shipping bins). Outdoors, where chests are spread all over, it takes from just [b]one chest[/b]: the Artisan Grabber you opened it from, or else the chest nearest to you. Small stacks of the same quality are combined, so 4 coffee beans in one chest and 3 in another still make a keg's worth.[/*]
[*][b]Keep machines filled[/b] (needs an Artisan Grabber in the building, which remembers your plan): whenever the grabber empties machines (overnight, and through the day as they finish) and whenever you close a chest there, empty machines are filled from the chests, never your backpack (outdoors, from the chest nearest the Artisan Grabber, or the chest you just closed). Drop coffee beans in a few at a time and a keg starts as soon as there are 5.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Auto-Petter[/b]
The game's own Auto-Petter, now with a crafting recipe. Put one in a barn or coop and it pets every animal there each morning: full happiness, half the friendship of petting by hand (pet them yourself as well for the rest).

[b]Storm Totem[/b]
Use it like a Rain Totem: tomorrow brings a thunderstorm, with about three times the usual lightning on the farm. Lightning rods catch strikes and turn them into batteries; without them, more strikes land on crops and trees, as in any storm. Festivals stay clear: used the day before one, the storm comes the day after the festival instead. On Ginger Island it brings an ordinary storm.

[line]

[size=5][b]Recipes[/b][/size]
All are known from the start and made at any crafting menu.
[list]
[*][b]Bulk Freezer (Keep Stars):[/b] 50 Wood, 5 Copper Bars[/*]
[*][b]Bulk Freezer (No Stars):[/b] 40 Wood, 5 Copper Bars[/*]
[*][b]Strongbox:[/b] 10 Iron Bars, 2 Gold Bars, 20 Hardwood[/*]
[*][b]Field Grabber:[/b] 30 Hardwood, 5 Gold Bars, 1 Battery Pack[/*]
[*][b]Greenhouse Grabber:[/b] 30 Hardwood, 5 Gold Bars, 1 Battery Pack[/*]
[*][b]Artisan Grabber:[/b] 30 Hardwood, 3 Gold Bars, 1 Oak Resin[/*]
[*][b]Auto-Petter:[/b] 20 Hardwood, 2 Gold Bars, 1 Battery Pack[/*]
[*][b]Storm Totem:[/b] 40 Wood, 1 Oak Resin, 1 Battery Pack[/*]
[/list]
[line]

[size=5][b]How to use[/b][/size]

[b]Making and placing the machines[/b]
[list=1]
[*]Open the Crafting tab of your game menu (the hammer icon). The PackRat machines are listed with the other craftables from day one.[/*]
[*]Gather the ingredients and craft the one you want.[/*]
[*]Select it in your toolbar and place it like a chest, by clicking an empty tile.[/*]
[*]To move one later, empty it, then hit it with a tool to pick it back up, the same as a chest.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Using a Bulk Freezer[/b]
[list=1]
[*]Choose your freezer: [b]Keep Stars[/b] (cream) to keep quality, or [b]No Stars[/b] (icy blue) to flatten everything into one stack per item.[/*]
[*]Place it anywhere, ideally in or near your kitchen. Cooking in the same building uses what's inside, just as it uses the fridge.[/*]
[*]Put in anything you want consolidated. Matching stacks merge straight away; in the No Stars freezer, starred items drop to normal quality first.[/*]
[*]In the No Stars freezer, the [b]Move in[/b] button under the PackRat button moves a whole group from your backpack: click it to see the groups and how many you're carrying, then click a group. It always takes two clicks, so it can't happen by accident, and anything that doesn't fit stays in your backpack with its stars.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Using a Strongbox[/b]
[list=1]
[*]Craft and place a Strongbox, then try to open it. The first time, you'll find your Strongbox Key taped to the lid.[/*]
[*]Keep the key anywhere in your backpack, then open the Strongbox. Without the key on you, you'll see "It's locked."[/*]
[*]Switch pages with the numbered tabs (1, 2, 3) on the left of the Strongbox menu. You can carry an item from one page to another: pick it up, click another page's tab, and drop it in. Hover a tab to see how full that page is.[/*]
[*]When you close it, the Strongbox shows its first page that has anything on it next time. Like any chest, it can only be picked up when every page is empty.[/*]
[*]Lost the key? Visit Clint at the Blacksmith: a replacement Strongbox Key is at the top of his shop for 2,500g whenever the key isn't in your backpack.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Setting up a Field Grabber[/b]
[list=1]
[*]Hold it and move around the farm: the quarter it would cover lights up green, with its name on a tag. Cross the middle of the farm and it switches quarters.[/*]
[*]Place it anywhere in the quarter you want. One per quarter is all you need.[/*]
[*]Go to bed. Next morning, the quarter's ripe crops, fruit, honey and the like are inside the grabber, and a message says how much was picked.[/*]
[*]Open it to collect. Empty it now and then: a full grabber stops collecting.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Setting up the Greenhouse and Artisan Grabbers[/b]
[list=1]
[*]Place a Greenhouse Grabber anywhere inside your greenhouse (or a shed of garden pots). It harvests the whole building each night.[/*]
[*]Place an Artisan Grabber anywhere inside the building that holds your machines. Everything that finishes, overnight or during the day, is waiting inside it, and the machines are empty and ready to refill.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Using the Machine Loader[/b]
[list=1]
[*]Stand in the building with your machines and press [b]K[/b] (or click Load in its Artisan Grabber).[/*]
[*]For each item, pick a machine from its dropdown, or leave it on Nothing. To set a whole kind at once, use a group row at the top, such as All vegetables; items you set yourself still go where you put them. Move rows up or down to set priority.[/*]
[*]Click [b]Fill[/b]. It takes from the chests there, never your backpack, so put anything you're carrying into a chest (such as the Artisan Grabber) first.[/*]
[*]Tick [b]Keep machines filled[/b] to have it top up the machines from the chests whenever the grabber empties them, and whenever you close a chest in the building. Your plan is remembered by the building's Artisan Grabber.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Labeling a chest[/b]
[list=1]
[*]Point your mouse at any chest and press [b]L[/b], or open it and click the label button on the right of the chest menu, the one showing "Aa" (or the chest's label, once it has one).[/*]
[*]Type up to 3 characters, such as "Win", "Fsh" or "B2", and click OK. To remove a label, clear the text and click OK.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Using the PackRat menu[/b]
[list=1]
[*]Press [b]P[/b], or click the PackRat button below the trash can on your backpack page, or in any chest.[/*]
[*]Pick a tab down the left side, or stay on Everything. Type in the search box to filter, for example "wine" or "blue".[/*]
[*]Hover any item to see its total, its quality breakdown and the chests it's in.[/*]
[*]Use the buttons under the search box to filter. Click one to open its list, then click the option you want:
[list]
[*][b]Show:[/b] Everything, Have or Missing. Items you have none of anywhere are faded. While another filter is on, Everything shows only what matches it.[/*]
[*][b]Quality:[/b] Any, Silver+, Gold+ or Iridium. Show: Missing with Quality: Iridium lists everything you have no iridium of.[/*]
[*][b]Where:[/b] Anywhere, or one place such as On you, Shed or Greenhouse.[/*]
[*][b]In:[/b] Everything, or one kind of storage: Chests, Strongboxes, Freezers, Fridges, Dressers, Grabbers, Junimo Chests, Backpack, Wearing, Hoppers & Bins, Museum or Bundles.[/*]
[*][b]Type:[/b] Any, or one type of item from the tab you're on: Vegetable, Fruit, Mushroom, Artifact, Geode, Legendary Fish, each artisan product (Wine, Jelly, Juice...) and more.[/*]
[*][b]Sort:[/b] Name, Count or Value (the sale price of one).[/*]
[/list][/*]
[*][b]To find a chest:[/b] click an item to pin its card, then click one of its chest rows. If that chest is in the area you're in, a "Here!" tag bobs over it; if it's elsewhere, the menu tells you where.[/*]
[*][b]To check your grabbers:[/b] click the last tab (the wine-red grabber). Each place lists its grabbers with how full they are; a red line means a quarter or building has none. Click a grabber to find it.[/*]
[*]Close the menu with [b]P[/b], [b]E[/b], [b]Esc[/b] or the red X.[/*]
[/list]
[line]

[size=5][b]Controls and settings[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]P:[/b] open or close the PackRat menu[/*]
[*][b]L[/b] (pointing at a chest): label it[/*]
[*][b]K:[/b] open the Machine Loader for the building you're in[/*]
[*][b]Moving the buttons:[/b] hold [b]Shift[/b] and drag any PackRat button (on the backpack page or in a chest) to where you want it. Shift + right-click puts it back.[/*]
[/list]
Settings live in [i]Mods/PackRat/config.json[/i], which appears after the first launch. Open it in Notepad with the game closed:
[list]
[*][b]OpenPackRat, LabelChest, OpenMachineLoader:[/b] the keys. Any key works, a combination such as "LeftShift + P", two choices such as "P, F7", or a controller button such as "LeftStick".[/*]
[*][b]VegetarianMode:[/b] set to true and the PackRat menu leaves out Smoked Fish entirely.[/*]
[*][b]ShowGrabberCoverage:[/b] set to false to turn off the green quarter highlight.[/*]
[*][b]ButtonOffsets:[/b] where you've dragged the buttons. No need to edit this by hand.[/*]
[/list]
[line]

[size=5][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Stardew Valley 1.6[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/2400]SMAPI[/url] 4.0 or later[/*]
[/list]No other mods needed, and no Harmony patches.

[size=5][b]Installing and updating[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*]Install SMAPI.[/*]
[*]Unzip this mod into your [i]Stardew Valley/Mods[/i] folder. When updating, replace the old PackRat folder (your config.json can stay).[/*]
[*]Launch the game through SMAPI.[/*]
[/list]Updating from 1.0: your Crop Grabbers become Field Grabbers (outdoors) or Greenhouse Grabbers (indoors) the next morning, keeping what's inside. A Greenhouse Grabber already outdoors keeps working as before (covering the whole outdoor area) until you pick it up, but can't be placed outdoors again; use a Field Grabber there instead.

[size=5][b]Uninstalling[/b][/size]
Empty your Bulk Freezers, Strongboxes and Grabbers [b]before[/b] removing the mod. Without it they become error items, and what's inside them may not be recoverable. Chest labels simply stop showing.

[line]

[size=5][b]Good to know[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Multiplayer:[/b] built with co-op in mind: grabbers run once, on the host, and each credits the experience to whoever placed it (or the host, if they're offline); two players can't open the same Strongbox page at once; each player finds their own Strongbox Key. It's been tested in single player only, so please report anything odd in co-op.[/*]
[*][b]Controller:[/b] the menus work with a gamepad cursor, but don't snap from slot to slot yet.[/*]
[*][b]Holding an item:[/b] PackRat's buttons won't open while you're holding an item on your cursor. Put it down first, so it can't get lost when the menu switches.[/*]
[*]Not counted in the PackRat menu: items on the ground, and items still inside machines.[/*]
[*]The missing list covers every object you can carry: crops, forage, fish, artisan goods, cooking, minerals, geodes, artifacts, resources, seeds, rings, books, quest items and so on. Clothing, tools, weapons and furniture show only when you own them.[/*]
[/list]
Found a bug or have an idea? Leave a comment in the Posts tab.

Manifest.Name: PackRat
Manifest.Description: Press P (or the PackRat button in your backpack or any chest) to see everything you have stored and everything you're still missing, with filters. Plus: two self-stacking Bulk Freezers, a 210-slot Strongbox that opens while its key is in your backpack, Field, Greenhouse and Artisan Grabbers that harvest and collect overnight, a Machine Loader that fills a whole shed of machines (K), a Storm Totem, a craftable Auto-Petter, and chest labels (L).
Manifest.Author: annan
